Package io.github.jspinak.brobot.tools.history

Class HistoryFileNamer

java.lang.Object
io.github.jspinak.brobot.tools.history.HistoryFileNamer
@Component public class HistoryFileNamer extends Object
Generates unique filenames for Brobot's visual history illustrations.

This component manages the naming convention for all illustration files generated during action execution. It ensures unique filenames while encoding important metadata like action types, target images, and analysis results. The naming system prevents filename collisions and makes illustrations easily searchable.

Filename structure patterns:

  • Basic: {prefix}_{action}_{imageNames}.png
  • Scene analysis: {prefix}_{action}_in-{sceneName}_{targetImages}_{analysisType}.png
  • With Find type: {prefix}_FIND_{findType}_{imageNames}.png

Key features:

  • Automatic uniqueness through FilenameAllocator integration
  • Metadata encoding in filename for easy identification
  • Support for multiple naming strategies based on action type
  • Configurable base path and prefix via BrobotProperties

Common naming components:

  • Action type: FIND, CLICK, CLASSIFY, etc.
  • Scene name: Name of the analyzed scene or "screenshot"
  • Target images: Underscore-separated list of searched images
  • Analysis descriptors: "classes", "scene", etc.

Thread safety: This component is thread-safe through its dependency on thread-safe FilenameAllocator for filename reservation.

  • Method Details

    • getSingleFilename

      public String getSingleFilename(ActionResult matches, ActionConfig actionConfig)
      Generates a single filename for the primary illustration of an action result.

      This method handles cases where matches may contain multiple or no SceneAnalyses. When SceneAnalyses are present, it uses the first one; otherwise, it falls back to generating a filename from match objects. This ensures every action gets an illustration filename regardless of analysis availability.

      Filename structure with SceneAnalysis:

      • Action name (FIND, CLICK, CLASSIFY, etc.)
      • "in-{SceneName}": scene identifier or "screenshot"
      • Target image names separated by underscores
      • Analysis type descriptor ("classes" for pixel classification, etc.)

      Usage note: For multiple SceneAnalyses, call getFilenameFromSceneAnalysis(io.github.jspinak.brobot.model.analysis.scene.SceneAnalysis, io.github.jspinak.brobot.action.ActionConfig, java.lang.String...) for each analysis to get individual filenames.

      Parameters:
      matches - action results containing search targets and analysis data
      actionConfig - configuration including the action type
      Returns:
      unique filename path for the illustration

    • getFilenameFromMatchObjects

      public String getFilenameFromMatchObjects(ActionResult matches, ActionConfig actionConfig)
      Generates a filename based on match objects when no scene analysis is available.

      Creates filenames by extracting state object names from all matches and combining them with the action type. This fallback method ensures illustrations can be saved even when detailed scene analysis isn't performed.

      The method aggregates unique state object names to avoid duplication in filenames, making them more readable and preventing excessively long names.

      Parameters:
      matches - action results containing matched objects
      actionConfig - configuration with action type information
      Returns:
      unique filename path constructed from match data

    • getFilenameFromSceneAnalysis

      public String getFilenameFromSceneAnalysis(SceneAnalysis sceneAnalysis, ActionConfig actionConfig, String... additionalDescription)
      Generates a detailed filename from scene analysis data with optional descriptors.

      Creates rich filenames that encode the complete context of an analysis: action type, scene name, target images, and any additional descriptors. This detailed naming helps identify illustrations at a glance and supports efficient searching through history files.

      The "in-{sceneName}" convention clearly indicates which scene was analyzed, while additional descriptors can specify analysis types like "classes" for classification results or "colorProfile" for color analysis.

      Parameters:
      sceneAnalysis - analysis results including scene and target information
      actionConfig - configuration with action type
      additionalDescription - optional descriptors appended to filename (e.g., "classes", "contours")
      Returns:
      unique filename path with encoded analysis metadata

    • getFilename

      public String getFilename(ActionConfig actionConfig, ObjectCollection... objectCollections)
      Generates a filename from multiple object collections.

      Processes multiple ObjectCollections to create comprehensive filenames that include all involved state images. Special handling for FIND actions includes the find type (e.g., FIND_ALL, FIND_FIRST) in the filename for better identification of search strategies.

      This method aggregates image names from all collections, making it ideal for complex operations involving multiple state objects or when comparing results across different object sets.

      Parameters:
      actionConfig - configuration including action type and find options
      objectCollections - variable number of collections containing state images
      Returns:
      unique filename incorporating all object collection data

    • getFilename

      public String getFilename(ActionType actionType, String name)
      Generates a simple filename with action type and custom name.

      Provides maximum flexibility by accepting a custom name string, useful for special cases where standard naming conventions don't apply. Common uses include debugging illustrations, custom analysis results, or user-specified illustration names.

      Parameters:
      name - custom name component for the filename
      action - action type to include in filename
      Returns:
      unique filename with action and custom name
